messages.content: my father found an old camera while cleaning a shelf. he also found a picture of the window in our old house. the picture made me remember sitting there after school.
a small picture can bring back more than what is on the page. what do you remember about sitting by that window?
i remember putting my books on the floor and waiting for my mother to come home. sometimes i read, and sometimes i just looked outside.
so the window was part of that waiting time. you can see the place in the picture and remember what you did there, even when those details are not in the picture itself.
my father can remember the same window because he put a new shelf near it. we both started talking about different parts of the room.
you each had a different reason to remember it. talking about both can help you learn more about the same place without either of you having to remember every detail.
say it simply.
you can remember different parts of the same room. talking about them can help each of you learn what the other can remember.
give me a question i can ask him.
what do you remember doing near that window?
i want to make a short note about the picture, but not say every detail i remember is in it.
this is a picture of the window in our old house. it makes me remember sitting there after school, with my books on the floor and time to look outside.
ask my last request simply.
write a short note about the picture, but do not say everything i remember can be seen in it.
i let my sister use my blanket while she had a rest on the sofa. now she has put it in her room. i want it back, but i do not know why she put it there.
you can ask for it without choosing a reason for why it moved. you could say: could i have my blanket back from your room? i would like to use it now.
keep my idea simple.
i let my sister use my blanket on the sofa. now it is in her room. i want it back, but i do not know why she put it there.
now give a kind request with that same idea.
could i have my blanket back? i think it is in your room, and i would like to use it.
i know it is there because i saw it. do not say i think.
could i have my blanket back from your room? i would like to use it now.
she says she put it there so nobody would sit on it. what can i answer?
thank you for keeping it out of the way. i would like it back now so i can use it.
does her reason make it her blanket?
no. keeping it in her room does not change whose blanket it is in this example. you let her use it, and you are now asking for it back.
write one sentence about the difference between using and keeping as your own.
you can use a blanket for a while, but that does not by itself make it your own.
write a story about a child drawing a person seen in a mirror. let someone ask whether there are two real people, and the child explain that it is the same person.

a child stood near a mirror and tried to draw what she saw. when her brother came in, he looked at the picture and asked why there were two people in the room. she said one was the person standing there and the other was how that person looked in the mirror. it was the same person in both parts of the picture. her brother stood next to her and looked again. now there were two real people near the mirror, so she needed more space on the page.
what changed when the brother came in?
before he came in, there was one real person near the mirror. after he came in, there were two. the picture of a person in the mirror did not itself add another real person to the room.
can you ask the child whether to count real people or people in the picture?
do you want to count the real people in the room or the people you can see in the whole drawing?
ask my request simply.
write a question asking whether the child is talking about real people or people in the picture.
now make the story shorter but keep the change from one to two real people.

a child drew herself near a mirror. her brother asked if the picture showed two real people. she said it was one person and what the mirror showed. then he stood near her, so there were now two real people in the room.
showed is okay, but can you end with the drawing still not finished?
when her brother stood near her, she looked at the empty part of the page. she would need to draw a little more before the picture was done.
there are eight coins in a container. i put three on the table. how many are still in the container?
five coins are still in the container, and three are on the table. there are still eight coins together.
now my brother puts two more coins into the container. those two were not part of my eight.
then there are seven coins in the container. the three on the table are still there, so the example now has ten coins together.
if he takes one coin from the table, how many are in each place?
there are seven in the container, two on the table, and one with your brother. there are still ten together in this example.
does taking the coin make it his now?
no. moving a coin into his hand does not by itself tell us whose it is. you would need to say whether it was given to him, or whether he was only holding it.
ask that question simply.
does taking the coin make it his own?
now i say he is only holding it while we count. give the whole number without leaving his coin out.
there are ten coins together: seven in the container, two on the table, and one that your brother is holding.
what if i only ask how many are on the table?
then the answer is two. the question about one place should not be answered with the number in all the places together.
i heard a song on the radio and wanted to tell my cousin about it, but i do not know the name. i remember a few words and how it sounds.
you can tell your cousin what you remember without saying you know the song name. do you want help writing a message asking whether they know it?
yes. i do not have the words to give you right now. i just want a short message i can add them to later.
i heard a song on the radio and cannot remember its name. if i send you the words i remember, could you tell me whether you know it?
why not write i found the song already?
because you have not said you found it. you are still asking for help finding out what it is. the message should keep that part open.
my cousin says i should sing the part i remember. i do not really want to try that yet.

you can choose whether you want to try. you could also send the words you remember first and say you do not want to sing it. asking for help does not mean you have to use only the way they first gave.
keep the reply simple.
you can send the words first if you do not want to sing. you could say: i would rather start with the words i remember.
now make a short reply with that choice.
i would rather send the words i remember first. maybe that will be enough to start.
if they do not know it, does that mean it was not a real song?
no. one person not knowing it does not tell you it was not real. you still know what you heard, even if you do not yet know its name.
write a story about a child washing cups and trying to count which cups are clean. one cup should be in the wrong group, and the child should check without starting everything over.

a child washed some cups and put them on one side of the table. another cup was already there, and the child put it with the clean group. her father asked whether she had washed that one too. she looked at it and remembered it had been there before she started. rather than washing every cup again, she put that one back near the soap and checked the clean group. then she washed it and added it to that group.
make my request simple.
write a story where a child puts one cup with the clean cups before knowing it is clean, then looks at that cup and washes it.
why did she not have to wash every cup again?
the problem was about one cup. if she knew the rest had been washed and nothing else changed, she could check just that cup for the story. one part that was not clear did not make every part wrong.
answer simply.
she knew which cups she had washed. she only needed to check and wash the cup that was already there, not choose that all her work was wrong.
give me a sentence about what she knew.
she knew she had washed the cups in one group, but she had not washed the cup that was already on the table.
can you make the end calm?
she washed the last cup and put it with the clean group. then she left the table ready for the meal.
keep the end simple.
she washed the last cup and put it with the clean cups. then she left the table ready for the meal.
my cousin and i had the same busy day together. after that i wanted to talk about it, but they wanted quiet. i felt like we should want the same thing because we did the same work.
people can do the same work and need different things after it. you may want to talk in order to think through the day, while your cousin may want a little quiet first.
keep my idea simple.
after our busy day together, i wanted to talk and my cousin wanted quiet. i thought doing the same work should make us want the same thing.
what can i ask without making them talk right now?
you could ask: would you like some quiet now and time to talk later, or would you rather leave the day alone for today?
make the question short.
would you like to talk later, after some quiet time?
they say tomorrow would be better. i still want to say one thing now, but i do not want to make them have the whole conversation.
you can ask whether one short thing is okay before saying it. if they say they really need quiet, you can write it down for yourself and talk tomorrow.
ask for one short thing.
could i tell you one short thing now, or would you rather keep the whole conversation for tomorrow?
why give them both choices?
it keeps clear that you are asking, not choosing for them. you can say what you want while still giving them room to answer.
answer simply.
you are asking what works for them, rather than saying they must talk now.
picoboi, write a story about a parent teaching a child to read a map. do not use it as information about my own family.

a parent put a map on the table and asked a child to find the library. the child found the road near their house, then moved a hand along it until they found the library. they talked about where they would turn before leaving together.
use simple words.
a parent and child looked at a map together. the child found their house, then the library. they looked at the road between them and talked about where to turn before leaving.
now do you know whether i am a parent?
no. the parent and child were part of the story you asked for. you have not told me whether that is part of your own life.
what if i now say i have one child?
then i can use that as something you told me in this conversation. it does not mean the map story really happened to you.
i do have one child. yesterday we read a book, not a map. keep that clear.
you told me you have one child and read a book together yesterday. the map was part of the made up story.
now ask me a question about the real reading, not the map.
what part of the book did you and your child read together?
ask what reading it felt like, without choosing a feeling for us.
what was it like reading the book together yesterday?
